samples_reviewed.question_text: Dividing 82 by 2 does not give an exact whole number, so 82 is an odd number. True or False?
5 ÷ 2 does not come out exactly, so 5 is an odd number. True or False?
Dividing 53 by 2 does not give an exact whole number, so 53 is an odd number. True or False?
35 can be divided into 2 equal parts, so 35 is an even number. True or False?
10 can be divided into 2 equal parts, so 10 is an even number. True or False?
60 cannot be divided into 2 equal whole parts, so 60 is an odd number. True or False?
Dividing 82 by 2 gives an exact whole number, so 82 is an even number. True or False?
65 ÷ 2 comes out exactly, so 65 is an even number. True or False?
Dividing 34 by 2 does not give an exact whole number, so 34 is an odd number. True or False?
25 cannot be divided into 2 equal whole parts, so 25 is an odd number. True or False?
52 ÷ 2 does not come out exactly, so 52 is an odd number. True or False?
Dividing 22 by 2 does not give an exact whole number, so 22 is an odd number. True or False?
Dividing 9 by 2 gives an exact whole number, so 9 is an even number. True or False?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency asks the pupil to distinguish even from odd. Each sampled item instead hands over a completed claim pairing a division result with a parity label and asks whether it holds, so the pupil is verifying somebody else's classification rather than producing one.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both parities are targeted and both phrasings of the halving test occur - dividing exactly into a whole number, and splitting into two equal parts - across single-digit numbers such as 5 and 9 and two-digit ones such as 65 and 82.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Each stem holds one number and one claim, the division involved is always halving, and the parity vocabulary is introduced within the sentence rather than assumed.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: All thirteen samples are true-or-false statements without exception. There is no item asking which number in a list is even, none asking a pupil to sort or label, and none that presents the halving visually, so a competency about distinguishing is delivered entirely through a binary guess with a fifty per cent floor.

competency_alignment.rationale: What changes between samples is the surface wording of the division test and which parity word is attached; the reasoning demanded is identical every time, so there is no progression within the node at all.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Numbers tested run from 5 up to 82, a range where halving is within Grade 2 reach while still requiring the pupil to think past the single-digit facts.
